title: Session 4: The "changed words" verses

series.title: What does the Quran say about the Bible?

opening_question: Some Quran verses say people "change words from their context" or write scripture with their own hands. Muslim scholars read this two ways. What does the Bible itself say about adding to, taking from, or twisting God's word?

steps.question: The Quran says a party "used to listen to the word of Allah, then used to change it". What does Jeremiah say about the scribes of his day?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: Do ye therefore desire that the Jews should believe you? yet a part of them heard the word of GOD, and then perverted it, after they had understood it, against their own conscience.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Have ye any hope that they will be true to you when a party of them used to listen to the word of Allah, then used to change it, after they had understood it, knowingly?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: And there are certainly some of them who read the scriptures perversely, that ye may think what they read to be really in the scriptures, yet it is not in the scripture; and they say, This is from GOD; but it is not from GOD: and they speak that which is false concerning GOD, against their own knowledge.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: And lo! there is a party of them who distort the Scripture with their tongues, that ye may think that what they say is from the Scripture, when it is not from the Scripture. And they say: It is from Allah, when it is not from Allah; and they speak a lie concerning Allah knowingly.

facts.text: Vain in Jeremiah 8:8 is sheqer: "an untruth". The BSB reads "the lying pen of the scribes".
In 3:78 Sale has some who "read the scriptures perversely"; Pickthall, some who "distort the Scripture with their tongues". Here the change is in the reading aloud.

steps.question: The Quran warns those who write scripture with their own hands and say it is from God. What does Moses command about adding to God's word, and what does Proverbs add?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: …And woe unto them, who transcribe corruptly the book of the law with their hands, and then say, This is from GOD: that they may sell it for a small price. Therefore woe unto them because of that which their hands have written; and woe unto them for that which they have gained.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Therefore woe be unto those who write the Scripture with their hands and then say, "This is from Allah," that they may purchase a small gain therewith. Woe unto them for that their hands have written, and woe unto them for that they earn thereby.

facts.text: Moses forbids both: "Ye shall not add unto the word" and "neither shall ye diminish ought from it". Add is yasaph: "to add or augment"; diminish is gara: "to scrape off".
Sale words 2:79 as those "who transcribe corruptly the book of the law with their hands"; Pickthall, "those who write the Scripture with their hands".

steps.question: The Quran says some "change words from their context". What does Paul say many do with the word of God, and what does Peter say the unlearned do with Paul's letters?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: Of the Jews there are some who pervert words from their places; and say, We have heard, and have disobeyed; and do thou hear without understanding our meaning, and look upon us: perplexing with their tongues, and reviling the true religion. But if they had said, We have heard, and do obey; and do thou hear, and regard us: certainly it were better for them, and more right. But GOD hath cursed them by reason of their infidelity; therefore a few of them only shall believe.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Some of those who are Jews change words from their context and say: "We hear and disobey; hear thou as one who heareth not" and "Listen to us!" distorting with their tongues and slandering religion. If they had said: "We hear and we obey: hear thou, and look at us" it had been better for them, and more upright. But Allah hath cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few.

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: Wherefore because they have broken their covenant, we have cursed them, and hardened their hearts; they dislocate the words of the Pentateuch from their places, and have forgotten part of what they were admonished; and thou wilt not cease to discover deceitful practices among them, except a few of them. But forgive them, and pardon them, for GOD loveth the beneficent.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: And because of their breaking their covenant, We have cursed them and made hard their hearts. They change words from their context and forget a part of that whereof they were admonished. Thou wilt not cease to discover treachery from all save a few of them. But bear with them and pardon them. Lo! Allah loveth the kindly.

facts.text: Corrupt is kapeleuo: "to retail", and by implication "to adulterate", like a peddler. Wrest is strebloo: "to wrench".
In 5:13 Sale writes "they dislocate the words of the Pentateuch from their places"; Pickthall, "They change words from their context". The Arabic names no book: Sale added "of the Pentateuch".

steps.question: What does the last chapter of the Bible warn anyone who adds to, or takes away from, the words of the book?

facts.text: Add is epitithemi: "to impose"; take away is aphaireo: "to remove". Revelation closes with the two warnings of Deuteronomy 4:2.

Copies differ here, and BibleChat shows it: the King James reads "book of life", the Ethiopian Canon and the BSB "tree of life". The Greek manuscripts have "tree"; the printed Greek the King James followed took "book" from the Latin.

Outside history, not Scripture: the Dead Sea Scrolls (copied about 250 BC to AD 68) hold parts of every Old Testament book except Esther, and thousands of Greek New Testament manuscripts survive, many older than the Quran: Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus were copied in the 300s, about 300 years before Muhammad. Readers can compare today's Bible with them.

steps.question: Paul says the Jews were trusted with "the oracles of God". If some did not believe, does that make God's faithfulness fail?

facts.text: Muslim scholars read these verses in two ways. Tahrif al-ma'na: the meaning was twisted in reading and explaining, and the text was kept. Tahrif al-lafz: the text itself was changed. Early commentators such as al-Tabari (died 923) often explain them the first way; Ibn Hazm (died 1064) argued for the second, and it became the more common view in later Islamic teaching.

steps.question: Living it out: Paul says "let God be true, but every man a liar". How should we handle God's word ourselves, according to these verses?

facts.text: "rightly dividing the word of truth"; "nor handling the word of God deceitfully".

es.title: Sesión 4: Los versículos de las «palabras cambiadas»
es.opening_question: Algunos versículos del Corán dicen que hay quienes «cambian las palabras de su contexto» o escriben la Escritura con sus propias manos. Los eruditos musulmanes lo leen de dos maneras. ¿Qué dice la Biblia misma de añadir, quitar o torcer la palabra de Dios?

steps.question: El Corán dice que un grupo «escuchaba la palabra de Alá y después la cambiaba». ¿Qué dice Jeremías de los escribas de su tiempo?
facts: "en vano" en Jeremías 8:8 es sheqer: «una mentira». La BSB inglesa dice «la pluma mentirosa de los escribas».
En 3:78 Sale habla de algunos que «leen las Escrituras perversamente»; Pickthall, de algunos que «tuercen la Escritura con sus lenguas». Aquí el cambio está en la lectura en voz alta.

steps.question: El Corán advierte a los que escriben la Escritura con sus propias manos y dicen que es de Dios. ¿Qué manda Moisés sobre añadir a la palabra de Dios, y qué añade Proverbios?
facts: Moisés prohíbe las dos cosas: "No añadiréis á la palabra" y "ni disminuiréis de ella". Añadir es yasaph: «añadir o aumentar»; disminuir es gara: «raspar».
Sale traduce 2:79 como los que «transcriben corruptamente el libro de la ley con sus manos»; Pickthall, «los que escriben la Escritura con sus manos».

steps.question: El Corán dice que algunos «cambian las palabras de su contexto». ¿Qué dice Pablo que hacen muchos con la palabra de Dios, y qué dice Pedro que hacen los indoctos con las cartas de Pablo?
facts: "mercaderes falsos" traduce kapeleuo: «vender al por menor», y por extensión «adulterar», como un buhonero. "tuercen" traduce strebloo: «retorcer».
En 5:13 Sale escribe «dislocan las palabras del Pentateuco de sus lugares»; Pickthall, «Cambian las palabras de su contexto». El árabe no nombra ningún libro: Sale añadió «del Pentateuco».

steps.question: ¿Qué advierte el último capítulo de la Biblia a cualquiera que añada o quite de las palabras del libro?
facts: Añadir es epitithemi: «imponer»; quitar es aphaireo: «sacar». Apocalipsis cierra con las dos advertencias de Deuteronomio 4:2: "Si alguno añadiere" y "si alguno quitare".

Aquí las copias difieren, y BibleChat lo muestra: la King James y la Reina-Valera dicen "libro de la vida", el Canon etíope y la BSB «árbol de la vida». Los manuscritos griegos tienen «árbol»; el griego impreso que siguió la King James tomó «libro» del latín.

Fuera de la Escritura, en la historia: los Rollos del Mar Muerto (copiados entre 250 a. C. y 68 d. C.) contienen partes de todos los libros del Antiguo Testamento menos Ester, y se conservan miles de manuscritos griegos del Nuevo Testamento, muchos más antiguos que el Corán: el Códice Sinaítico y el Códice Vaticano se copiaron en el siglo IV, unos 300 años antes de Mahoma. Cualquiera puede comparar la Biblia de hoy con ellos.

steps.question: Pablo dice que a los judíos les fue confiada "la palabra de Dios". Si algunos no creyeron, ¿hace eso que falle la fidelidad de Dios?
facts: "palabra" aquí traduce logion: «un dicho (de Dios)».

Los eruditos musulmanes leen estos versículos de dos maneras. Tahrif al-ma'na: el sentido se torció al leer y explicar, y el texto se conservó. Tahrif al-lafz: el texto mismo se cambió. Comentaristas antiguos como al-Tabari (murió en 923) suelen explicarlos de la primera manera; Ibn Hazm (murió en 1064) defendió la segunda, que llegó a ser la más común en la enseñanza islámica posterior.

steps.question: Para vivirlo: Pablo dice "sea Dios verdadero, mas todo hombre mentiroso". ¿Cómo debemos manejar nosotros la palabra de Dios, según estos versículos?
facts: "que traza bien la palabra de verdad"; "ni adulterando la palabra de Dios".

remember: Jeremías: "en vano se cortó la pluma, por demás fueron los escribas".
"No añadiréis á la palabra que yo os mando"
Pablo y Pedro advierten contra los que adulteran o tuercen las Escrituras.
"sea Dios verdadero, mas todo hombre mentiroso"

de.title: Teil 4: Die Verse von den »veränderten Worten«
de.opening_question: Einige Verse des Korans sagen, Leute »verdrehen die Worte von ihrer Stelle« oder schreiben die Schrift mit eigenen Händen. Muslimische Gelehrte lesen das auf zwei Weisen. Was sagt die Bibel selbst über das Hinzufügen, Wegnehmen oder Verdrehen von Gottes Wort?

steps.question: Der Koran sagt, eine Gruppe »hörte das Wort Allahs und veränderte es dann«. Was sagt Jeremia über die Schriftgelehrten seiner Zeit?
facts: Das Wort in Jeremia 8,8 ist sheqer: »eine Unwahrheit«. Luther übersetzt: "Ist's doch eitel Lüge, was die Schriftgelehrten setzen".
In 3,78 hat Sale einige, die »die Schriften verkehrt lesen«; Pickthall einige, die »die Schrift mit ihren Zungen verdrehen«. Hier liegt die Veränderung im lauten Vorlesen.

steps.question: Der Koran warnt die, die die Schrift mit eigenen Händen schreiben und sagen, sie sei von Gott. Was gebietet Mose über das Hinzufügen zu Gottes Wort, und was fügen die Sprüche hinzu?
facts: Mose verbietet beides: "Ihr sollt nichts dazutun" und "sollt auch nichts davontun". Dazutun ist yasaph: »hinzufügen, vermehren«; davontun ist gara: »abschaben«.
Sale übersetzt 2,79 als die, »die das Buch des Gesetzes mit ihren Händen verfälscht abschreiben«; Pickthall: »die, die die Schrift mit ihren Händen schreiben«.

steps.question: Der Koran sagt, manche »verdrehen die Worte von ihrer Stelle«. Was tun nach Paulus viele mit dem Wort Gottes, und was tun nach Petrus die Ungelehrigen mit den Briefen des Paulus?
facts: "verfälschen" steht für kapeleuo: »im Kleinen verkaufen«, und daher »panschen«, wie ein Hausierer. "verdrehen" steht für strebloo: »verrenken«.

In 5,13 schreibt Sale »sie verrücken die Worte des Pentateuch von ihren Stellen«; Pickthall: »Sie verdrehen die Worte von ihrer Stelle«. Das Arabische nennt kein Buch: Sale fügte »des Pentateuch« hinzu.

steps.question: Wovor warnt das letzte Kapitel der Bibel jeden, der zu den Worten des Buches etwas hinzufügt oder davon wegnimmt?
facts: Dazusetzen ist epitithemi: »auflegen«; davontun ist aphaireo: »wegnehmen«. Die Offenbarung schließt mit den zwei Warnungen aus 5. Mose 4,2: "So jemand dazusetzt" und "so jemand davontut".

Hier unterscheiden sich die Abschriften, und BibleChat zeigt es: die King James liest »Buch des Lebens«, Luther "Holz des Lebens", der äthiopische Kanon und die BSB »Baum des Lebens«. Die griechischen Handschriften haben »Baum«; der gedruckte griechische Text, dem die King James folgte, nahm »Buch« aus dem Lateinischen.

Außerhalb der Schrift, aus der Geschichte: Die Schriftrollen vom Toten Meer (abgeschrieben etwa 250 v. Chr. bis 68 n. Chr.) enthalten Teile jedes alttestamentlichen Buches außer Ester, und Tausende griechische Handschriften des Neuen Testaments sind erhalten, viele älter als der Koran: der Codex Sinaiticus und der Codex Vaticanus wurden im 4. Jahrhundert abgeschrieben, etwa 300 Jahre vor Mohammed. Jeder kann die heutige Bibel mit ihnen vergleichen.

steps.question: Paulus sagt, den Juden sei vertraut worden, "was Gott geredet hat". Wenn manche nicht glaubten, hört dann Gottes Treue auf?
facts: Das Wort ist logion: »ein Ausspruch (Gottes)«.

Muslimische Gelehrte lesen diese Verse auf zwei Weisen. Tahrif al-ma'na: der Sinn wurde beim Lesen und Erklären verdreht, der Text blieb erhalten. Tahrif al-lafz: der Text selbst wurde verändert. Frühe Ausleger wie al-Tabari (gestorben 923) erklären sie oft auf die erste Weise; Ibn Hazm (gestorben 1064) vertrat die zweite, und sie wurde in der späteren islamischen Lehre die häufigere Sicht.

steps.question: Für das Leben: Paulus sagt, "daß Gott sei wahrhaftig und alle Menschen Lügner". Wie sollen wir nach diesen Versen selbst mit Gottes Wort umgehen?
facts: "der da recht teile das Wort der Wahrheit"; "fälschen auch nicht Gottes Wort".

remember: Jeremia: "Ist's doch eitel Lüge, was die Schriftgelehrten setzen."
"Ihr sollt nichts dazutun zu dem, was ich euch gebiete"
Paulus und Petrus warnen vor denen, die die Schriften verfälschen oder verdrehen.
"daß Gott sei wahrhaftig und alle Menschen Lügner"
